Loading the child into a local before the recursive Traverse call puts the object load ahead of the argument loads as retail (358 to 23). Remaining: VC6 cross-jumps the VisitChild(1) and VisitChild(0) recursive-call tails (retail keeps them apart and instead merges two slot-2 call tails), and loads childX after push half in that block. Worse: the != 8 arm first (271), child local shared by both calls (616), tail assigned in both arms (215), inline childX/childZ ternaries (no change). The tail-merge choice is a dead end so far: distinct argument expressions in either call (inline ternaries in one or both), a QuadTreeNode* local or a shared __forceinline helper for the slot-2 call and braced if/else all compile to the same 23; a result local or tail assignment in both arms gives 693, the ternary return 358 (3026 B), a < 8 inverted test 422. The merged pair is the last VisitChild of the third and fourth groups (children 1 and 0, whose tails differ only in childZ); retail's Traverse tails for that pair are identical from push half yet unmerged, so VC6 appears to cross-jump only one predecessor pair of the join and its pick depends on IR order we have not reproduced.
